title: Fixed Round Niche Tower and Centre Ladder Cutaway
description: One newly authored whole regional dovecote-inspired architectural cutaway. A continuous thick curved masonry wall encloses a circular floor and contains actual inward-facing blind nesting recesses within its thickness, with a separate ground-level doorway passing completely through the retained side. One complete conical roof shell rises to a real open narrow top throat. The front quarter of the wall and roof is deliberately removed and its finite section faces closed to expose the interior. A complete central timber axle stands in a full floor foot and upper wall-to-wall bearing beam; two full radial arms connect that axle to one whole inclined ladder with two stiles and complete rungs. All members remain in one fixed display pose. This whole internal radial-access arrangement and curved blind-cell wall are not a freestanding nesting box multiplied or a silo recoloured, and no old tower, roof, nest box or ladder mesh is imported. Unlike the deep ice-storage pit under a tapering vault, the whole accessible-looking floor here is at ground datum and the retained wall itself houses many blind recesses. Three opaque solid PBR roles, metres Z up, full horizontal envelope centred. One architectural module zero scenes. Empty stylised historical-inspired artwork only: no birds, eggs, species suitability, husbandry, ecological effect, hygiene, animal welfare, precise historical reconstruction, ladder rotation, human access, roof thrust, load, structure, manufacturing or engineering safety capability. Rigging animation and interaction not made or verified.
